Attributed ASTIS-authored background restatement for fixed PBPS C.1 density/closedness invocation; not a printed standalone source theorem.
Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel structure, including rank zero. Let μ be any probability measure on E and η>0. For independent X∼μ and G∼N(0,I), define the actual joint law J of (X,X+√η G) and its second marginal ν=J.snd. There exists one genuine real linear partial gradient operator D₀ from scalar L²(ν) to E-valued L²(ν), with norm-dense domain, closability and a closed graph for its operator closure. For every scalar class u and vector class v in these two actual L² spaces, (u,v) lies in D₀.graph if and only if there exists a globally C∞ compactly supported real function f with u=f ν-almost everywhere and v=∇f ν-almost everywhere. The gradient is the actual inverse-Riesz Fréchet derivative. No finite moment, input density, potential, integrability, normalizer or gradient-domain certificate is supplied. This is authored background for the paper's density/closedness invocation, not its full rough-input B.13 theorem.
Remaining: Actual Gaussian outer marginal nu=J.snd admits a dense genuine smooth-compact gradient graph, is closable, and has closed closure. No literal Tf graph membership, arbitrary rough L2 smoothing estimate, Gamma/half-turn/main/errors/cost or actual-input composition is proved.
theorem gaussian_marginal_gradient_closable
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (μ : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) :
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1, p.1 + Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    ∃ D : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 ν,
      Dense (D.domain : Set (Lp ℝ 2 ν)) ∧ D.IsClosable ∧ D.closure.IsClosed ∧
      ∀ (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) (v : Lp E 2 ν), (u,v) ∈ D.graph ↔
        ∃ f : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ f ∧ HasCompactSupport f ∧
          u =ᵐ[ν] f ∧ v =ᵐ[ν] gradient f

Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with its norm and Borel measurable structure; zero dimension is allowed. Let μ be any probability measure on E and let η > 0. Independently draw x with law μ and g with the centered identity-covariance Gaussian law on E. Define J as the pushforward of μ × stdGaussian(E) by (x,g) ↦ (x,x + √η g), and let ν be the second marginal of J, the actual law of x + √η g.

There exists one real linear partial operator D from scalar L²(ν) to E-valued L²(ν). Its domain is a real linear subspace of scalar L²(ν) and is norm-dense. D is closable, and its operator closure D̄ has a closed graph. For every u in scalar L²(ν) and every v in E-valued L²(ν), (u,v) belongs to the actual graph of D if and only if there exists a globally C∞ compactly supported function f:E→ℝ such that u=f ν-almost everywhere and v=∇f ν-almost everywhere. Here ∇f is the genuine gradient obtained by applying the inverse real Riesz identification to the Fréchet derivative of f; both equalities use the same ν and mean equality of representatives of the L² classes.

Thus dom(D) consists exactly of scalar L² classes represented by globally smooth compactly supported functions, and D maps such a class to the ν-almost-everywhere class of its gradient. The existential assertion includes well-definedness on these classes. Closability means the norm closure of this graph remains single-valued. Equivalently, whenever a sequence of graph pairs converges in the product L² norm to (0,v), v=0. The graph of D̄ is the norm closure of the graph of D: its elements are limits (u,v) of sequences ([f_n],[∇f_n]) with f_n globally smooth and compactly supported. It is this closure graph that is closed; the statement does not assert that D itself is closed or that dom(D̄) contains every scalar L² class.

No moment, density, potential, extra regularity, or gradient-domain premise on μ is assumed. No conditional-integral domain claim, energy estimate, mixing bound, query-cost estimate, or quantitative constant is asserted.

# Genuine gradient domain of the actual Gaussian marginal

Authored full-space background for PBPS arXiv:2609.06905v1 Appendix C.1,
which reduces B.13 to smooth compact tests using density and closedness.
The actual outer law is the second marginal of the independent Gaussian
augmentation. Its positive C2 density, L1 property and normalization are
derived inside the proof, before invoking the existing weighted gradient.

Any probability input and finite real Hilbert/rank-zero extensions are
explicit. This constructs the genuine smooth-compact graph, a dense domain,
closability and closed closure on the outer law. It does not assert literal
Tf membership, the full rough-input estimate, Gamma, mixing or query costs.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.GaussianMarginalGradient

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace ContDiff Topology

noncomputable section
set_option autoImplicit false

theorem gaussian_marginal_gradient_closable
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (μ : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) :
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1, p.1 + Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    ∃ D : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 ν,
      Dense (D.domain : Set (Lp ℝ 2 ν)) ∧ D.IsClosable ∧ D.closure.IsClosed ∧
      ∀ (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) (v : Lp E 2 ν), (u,v) ∈ D.graph ↔
        ∃ f : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ f ∧ HasCompactSupport f ∧
          u =ᵐ[ν] f ∧ v =ᵐ[ν] gradient f := by
  let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
    (fun p : E × E => (p.1, p.1 + Real.sqrt η • p.2))
  let ν := J.snd
  change ∃ D : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 ν,
    Dense (D.domain : Set (Lp ℝ 2 ν)) ∧ D.IsClosable ∧ D.closure.IsClosed ∧
      ∀ (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) (v : Lp E 2 ν), (u,v) ∈ D.graph ↔
        ∃ f : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ f ∧ HasCompactSupport f ∧
          u =ᵐ[ν] f ∧ v =ᵐ[ν] gradient f
  let C := ((Real.sqrt (2*Real.pi*η))⁻¹)^Module.finrank ℝ E
  let Z := fun y : E => ∫ x, Real.exp (-‖y-x‖^2/(2*η)) ∂μ
  let ρ := fun y : E => C*Z y
  let W := fun y : E => -Real.log (ρ y)
  have hpair : Measurable (fun p : E × E =>
      (p.1, p.1 + Real.sqrt η • p.2)) := by fun_prop
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure J := Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map hpair.aemeasurable
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map measurable_snd.aemeasurable
  have hmap : ν = (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => p.1 + Real.sqrt η • p.2) :=
    Measure.map_map measurable_snd hpair
  obtain ⟨hdensity,hpos,hZ,hW⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianConvolutionRegularity.gaussian_convolution_potential_c2 μ hη
  have hνdensity : ν = (volume : Measure E).withDensity
      (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (ρ y)) := hmap.trans hdensity
  have hρ : Continuous ρ := continuous_const.mul hZ.continuous
  have hnn : 0 ≤ᵐ[(volume : Measure E)] ρ :=
    Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun y => (hpos y).le
  have hmass : (∫⁻ y, ENNReal.ofReal (ρ y) ∂(volume : Measure E)) = 1 := by
    have hm := congrArg (fun m : Measure E => m Set.univ) hνdensity
    rw [withDensity_apply _ MeasurableSet.univ] at hm
    simpa only [measure_univ,Measure.restrict_univ] using hm.symm
  have hI : Integrable ρ (volume : Measure E) :=
    (lintegral_ofReal_ne_top_iff_integrable hρ.aestronglyMeasurable hnn).mp
      (by rw [hmass]; exact ENNReal.one_ne_top)
  have hnorm : (∫ y, ρ y ∂(volume : Measure E)) = 1 :=
    ENNReal.ofReal_eq_one.mp ((ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal hI hnn).trans hmass)
  have hexp (y : E) : Real.exp (-W y) = ρ y := by
    dsimp only [W]
    rw [neg_neg,Real.exp_log (hpos y)]
  have hWI : Integrable (fun y => Real.exp (-W y)) (volume : Measure E) := by
    simpa only [hexp] using hI
  have htilt : (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun y => -W y) = ν := by
    rw [Measure.tilted]
    simp_rw [hexp]
    rw [hnorm]
    simpa only [div_one] using hνdensity.symm
  rw [← htilt]
  exact WeightedGradient.compact_gradient_closable W
    (hW.of_le (by norm_num)) hWI

end
end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.GaussianMarginalGradient
